project.name: Acme Shop
project.tagline: A small online shop: a Python API, a shop core and a React storefront.
project.overview:
Acme Shop lets people browse products, fill a cart and pay.

The server is split so that web handling, shop rules and storage each live in one place. The storefront is a separate React app that only talks to the API.

roles.name: Conductor
roles.meaning: Starts things and calls other files in order: entry points, CLIs, servers, scripts, build steps.

roles.name: Rulebook
roles.meaning: Defines what things must look like: types, schemas, interfaces, base classes, constants, registries. Does little work itself.

roles.name: Worker
roles.meaning: Does the actual work: the core logic, algorithms and transformations.

roles.name: Guard
roles.meaning: Checks something and refuses or stops when it is wrong: validation, auth, permissions, limits.

roles.name: Storekeeper
roles.meaning: Saves and loads data: databases, caches, files, queues, migrations.

roles.name: Courier
roles.meaning: Talks to the outside world: HTTP clients, API adapters, SDK wrappers, messaging.

roles.name: Analyst
roles.meaning: Measures and reports: metrics, logging, statistics, reports, charts.

roles.name: Face
roles.meaning: What a user sees: UI components, pages, views, templates, styles.

roles.name: Settings
roles.meaning: A file of settings or records that code reads.

roles.name: Helper
roles.meaning: Small shared utilities and package markers.

roles.name: Test
roles.meaning: Automated test that checks other files still behave as before.

parts.name: API layer
parts.role: Turns HTTP requests into calls on the core
parts.summary: The API layer receives web requests, checks who is asking and that the body looks right, then hands the work to the core. It never decides prices or stock rules itself. It only shapes the answer back into JSON.

parts.name: Shop core
parts.role: The rules of the shop: carts, prices, checkout
parts.summary: Everything the shop actually does lives here. Adding to a cart, working out the total, reserving stock and charging a card are plain functions with no knowledge of HTTP.

parts.name: Data store
parts.role: Saves and loads products, carts and orders
parts.summary: One small layer owns every SQL statement. The core asks for a product or saves an order and never sees a connection.

parts.name: Web app
parts.role: The pages a shopper clicks through
parts.summary: A React single-page app: product list, cart, checkout. It talks to the API through one typed client.

problems.title: Every request needs the same setup before any handler runs
problems.without: Each route would repeat logging, login checks and error handling, and they would drift apart.
problems.fix: app.py builds the app once and installs middleware.py, so every route gets logging and the login check for free.

problems.title: Shoppers need a URL for each thing they can do
problems.without: Without routes the core functions cannot be reached from a browser.
problems.fix: One router file per area (products, cart, orders). Each handler is a few lines that call the core and shape the result.

problems.title: Clients and the server must agree on the shape of the data
problems.without: A typo in a field name would only show up as a broken page.
problems.fix: schemas.py declares every body once and rejects bad input; pagination.py keeps list responses uniform.

problems.title: Failures need one vocabulary, and settings one home
problems.without: Random exceptions become 500 errors and settings get read in twenty places.
problems.fix: errors.py defines the deliberate errors, auth.py signs and checks tokens, config.py reads settings once.

problems.title: Shoppers must be able to find products
problems.without: A long list with no search is unusable past a few dozen items.
problems.fix: catalog.py ranks products by name and tag matches and returns one page at a time.

problems.title: A cart total must be right, every time
problems.without: Rounding, stock limits and promo codes would give different totals on different pages.
problems.fix: cart.py owns the rules for changing a cart; pricing.py is the only place that computes money.

problems.title: Placing an order touches many systems and must not half-happen
problems.without: If the card is charged but the order is not saved, the shopper pays for nothing.
problems.fix: checkout.py runs the steps in order and undoes stock holds on failure; payments.py and mailer.py wrap the outside services.

problems.title: The team needs to see how the shop is doing
problems.without: Without counters, problems are found by shoppers first.
problems.fix: metrics.py counts orders and failures and exposes a snapshot.

problems.title: The database must exist and be reachable
problems.without: Each module would open its own connection and disagree about the schema.
problems.fix: connection.py shares one connection with transactions; tables.py and the migration create the schema.

problems.title: The core should not know SQL
problems.without: SQL scattered through business code is hard to change and hard to test.
problems.fix: One module per kind of record: products, carts, orders.

problems.title: The app has to start and be built
problems.fix: main.tsx mounts the app, App.tsx picks the page, vite.config.ts builds it.

problems.title: Pages should not each talk to the server their own way
problems.without: Every page would parse errors and hold its own copy of the cart.
problems.fix: client.ts is the one place that calls the API; useCart.ts shares cart state.

problems.title: Shoppers need screens for browsing, the cart and paying
problems.fix: One page component per screen plus a small Money component for prices.

stories.title: A shopper searches for a product
stories.summary: A search text goes in; one ranked page of products comes out.

steps.text: The app starts, mounts the routers and logs every request.
The products router reads the search text and page number.
The catalog scores each product against the words in the search.
The database layer returns the matching rows.
The response is shaped by the ProductOut schema.

stories.title: A shopper adds an item to the cart
stories.summary: The cart rules check stock and update the saved cart.

steps.text: The login check runs before the handler.
The cart route validates the body.
The core checks stock and changes the cart.

stories.title: A shopper checks out
stories.summary: From the checkout form to a saved order and an emailed receipt.

steps.text: The checkout page collects the address and card token.
The client sends the order to the API.
The orders route hands the cart to checkout.
Checkout prices the cart, holds stock and charges the card.
The order is saved and a receipt is sent.

items.name: router
